subject: Chemistry
question: Consider the energy diagram shown below which represents the activation of the "hot pack" as seen in lab. The hot pack was at room temperature, and after it was "activated" it produced significant heat. What is represented by the point marked "A" on the diagram? <image 1> Point A represents the hot pack _____

options.A: As it is activated: The hot pack is at its peak energy state.
options.B: Before it is activated: The hot pack is at its lowest energy state.
options.C: As it is activated: Energy is added to "start" the hot pack to give off heat.
options.D: Before it is activated: The hot pack loses heat overall because the surroundings get warmer.
options.E: After it is activated: The hot pack has lost heat as a result of the activation.
options.F: As it is activated: The hot pack loses heat to activate.
options.G: After it is activated: The hot pack has less potential energy after it is activated.
options.H: Before it is activated: The hot back is highest in energy before it is activated.
options.I: After it is activated: The hot pack's energy remains the same.
options.J: Before it is activated: The hot pack has more potential energy.
